recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. Future changes to Medication packaging or ingredient strength should be handled under the later Medication issue family, not by reopening this already-applied STU3 cleanup.
issue_request: FHIR-13879 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 Pharmacy request to add clearer descriptions for Medication.amount and Medication.ingredient.amount, add examples, remove medication.preparedInstructions, and, after a later Pharmacy vote, retain Medication.status while improving its definitions/descriptions and examples of use.
initial_application: Historical commit 2559032b9b1cd17a3f528abbe59749fff309ed69 applied GF/FHIR-13879 Medication spreadsheet and example changes, including amount wording and removal of old prepared-dose/prepared-instructions source text. Historical commit eddae4c6adc0a38d7c292dfa6f82cc15e75e194e then applied the November 2017 decision to keep Medication.status and expanded the status comment.
additional_context: Medication is active and approved in source/fhir.ini. The current source has moved from the 2017 spreadsheet model to source/medication/structuredefinition-Medication.xml, and later final Pharmacy decisions changed the original amount model: FHIR-17375 renamed Medication.ingredient.amount to Medication.ingredient.strength and fixed definitions, while FHIR-46416 replaced the separate package amount concept with Medication.packageSize.numberOfItems and amountPerItem.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active Medication source retains the expanded status explanation, defines current packageSize and ingredient.strength guidance, has no non-Archive Medication.amount, Medication.ingredient.amount, or preparedInstruction remnants, and includes active examples using status and ingredient strength.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive with Modification issue changed Medication.ingredient.amount to Medication.ingredient.strength and fixed definitions, explaining why the current source should not still expose ingredient.amount.
Later Applied/Persuasive with Modification issue replaced the package amount/totalVolume concept with Medication.packageSize and its children.
Later Medication ingredient clarification refined current narrative and comments about ingredients, strength, and packaging.
